title: Review thread
description: A versioned workspace review thread. Unknown JSON-compatible properties are preserved for forward extensibility. Application validation additionally requires ordered ranges, real calendar dates, and distinct comment IDs.

schemaVersion.description: Only version 1 is supported. Other versions must not be rewritten.

revision.description: Optimistic concurrency revision. New unsaved threads use 0; the first save commits 1, and each successful save increments by one. Saves and deletes must compare the expected revision under an exclusive lock.

path.description: A confined workspace-relative POSIX path. Spaces and Unicode are supported. Absolute paths, drive syntax, colons, backslashes, control characters, empty segments, and dot or dot-dot segments are forbidden.

comments.description: The initial comment and every reply in conversation order. Comment IDs must be unique within the thread; the application checks this constraint.

metadata.description: Reserved extensibility space for JSON-compatible integration metadata. Readers preserve unknown metadata and other unknown properties.

uuid.description: A UUID with version 1 through 8 and the standard variant. Storage uses the lowercase UUID followed by .json as the canonical safe filename.

timestamp.description: An RFC 3339 timestamp with uppercase T and Z and no leap-second notation; application validation also checks calendar dates.

position.description: A zero-based line and zero-based UTF-16 code-unit offset within that line; line terminators are not part of the character count.

range.description: Zero-based UTF-16 range with an exclusive end. End must not precede start; this cross-field constraint is checked by the application. An empty range can anchor an empty line.

snapshot.description: Exact source excerpt, including line endings, captured when the thread was created or explicitly reattached. Automatic relocation does not replace it.

before.description: Original context immediately before the excerpt, used for conservative relocation.

after.description: Original context immediately after the excerpt, used for conservative relocation.

stale.description: True when the saved source selection cannot be matched unambiguously or the current source cannot be verified. Check the current file before relying on this range.

body.description: Nonblank plain text with no arbitrary length limit.
